blocks.x: As part of its Housing Accelerator Fund work, the City of Winnipeg changed its zoning by-laws on June 26, 2025 to allow two-, three- and four-unit homes as of right in many neighbourhoods. Height, setback and landscaping rules still apply. For owners looking to convert a house to a duplex in Winnipeg, that opens new ways to add rental income.
Here's how the main options compare, and what to look for in a builder before you start.
Your options: duplex, triplex or suite

What it is
Typical fit

Owner-occupied homes and rentals with good basement height

R1 or R2 lots with a single-family home
Dividing a house into two or three units
Larger older homes in mature neighbourhoods, where zoning allows

blocks.x: What every option needs

**Zoning that allows it.** Rules depend on your lot's zoning and neighbourhood. Some uses may be allowed outright and others need a conditional use approval. The City's suites page allows only one attached or detached suite on a single-family property. Check the current Winnipeg Zoning By-law or ask the City before you design.

**Building permits.** New suites must meet the Manitoba Building Code, including a smoke-tight barrier and fire protection between units, smoke and CO alarms, egress windows, ceiling height, sound control, and heating and ventilation. A secondary suite needs [a development permit and a building permit](/blog/secondary-suite-rules-winnipeg), plus separate electrical and plumbing permits.

**A duplex or triplex is a different approval.** The City's [change-of-use building permit form](https://legacy.winnipeg.ca/ppd/Documents/permits/Change-of-Use-Single-Two-Family-Dwelling-Building-Permit-Application-Form.pdf) covers two-family homes, triplexes and fourplexes. It asks whether you need a development permit, and wants floor plans with fire and sound separation details between units. Ask the City which route fits your lot.
**Utilities and services.** Plumbing, electrical capacity, water and sewer connections can drive costs, especially for detached suites.
**Parking and access.** Check whether parking is required, and how tenants will get to the unit.
Basement suites: a common starting point
Many Winnipeg homes have basements that can become legal suites, though a suite has to meet more rules than an ordinary [basement development](/services/basement-renovations). Watch for:
**Ceiling height** and beams or ducts that lower it
**Egress windows** large enough for bedrooms. New openings in a foundation wall call for engineered drawings
**Moisture and foundation cracks,** common in older homes on [clay soil](/blog/clay-soil-basement-cracks-winnipeg). Active leaks or cracks go to a specialist first
**A smoke-tight barrier, fire protection** and the exits the suite needs
**Sound control** between the suite and the main floor
Choosing a builder for a rental project in Winnipeg
Look for a builder who:
Can give references for **permitted** suite work, which you can check in the [City's permit search](/blog/check-permit-history-winnipeg-house).
Can walk you through zoning and permit steps before pricing.
Provides a detailed written quote with allowances clearly listed.
Can be looked up through [WCB's clearance search](/blog/how-to-check-a-contractors-wcb-clearance-manitoba) and the Companies Office.
Gives realistic timelines, including permit review time.
The bottom line
Adding a unit can add rental income to a property you already own and help Winnipeg's housing supply. Start with zoning, then design for code.

This is general information, not legal advice. Confirm the rules for your lot with the City.
